conceptBreakdown.title: 3.1 Heat Capacities & Mayer's Relation

summaryBox.title: Heat Capacities
summaryBox.takeaway: C_v = (∂U/∂T)_V ⟹ ΔU = n C_v,m ΔT. C_p = (∂H/∂T)_P ⟹ ΔH = n C_p,m ΔT. Mayer's: C_p,m - C_v,m = R.

conceptBreakdown.content:
• **Isochoric Heat Capacity ($C_v$)**: $\mathbf{C_v = \left( \frac{\partial U}{\partial T} \right)_V \implies \Delta U = n C_{v,m} \Delta T}$
• **Isobaric Heat Capacity ($C_p$)**: $\mathbf{C_p = \left( \frac{\partial H}{\partial T} \right)_P \implies \Delta H = n C_{p,m} \Delta T}$
• **Mayer's Relation (Ideal Gas)**: $\mathbf{C_{p,m} - C_{v,m} = R}$ (For $n$ moles: $C_p - C_v = nR$).

conceptBreakdown.codeSnippet:
DEGREE OF FREEDOM & HEAT CAPACITIES
                      
   GAS MOLECULARITY           f    C_v,m     C_p,m     γ = C_p / C_v
   Monatomic (He, Ne, Ar)     3    3/2 R     5/2 R     5/3 ≈ 1.67
   Diatomic (N₂, O₂, CO)      5    5/2 R     7/2 R     7/5 = 1.40
   Non-linear Triatomic (H₂O) 6    3 R       4 R       4/3 ≈ 1.33
conceptBreakdown.content: Each quadratic translational and rotational degree of freedom contributes $\frac{1}{2}RT$ to molar internal energy.

conceptBreakdown.heading: 3.3 Kirchhoff’s Law (Temperature Dependence of Δ_r H°)
conceptBreakdown.title: 3.3 Kirchhoff’s Law (Temperature Dependence of Δ_r H°)
conceptBreakdown.content:
The variation of reaction enthalpy ($\Delta_r H^\circ$) with temperature:

$$\mathbf{\Delta_r H^\circ (T_2) - \Delta_r H^\circ (T_1) = \Delta C_p^\circ (T_2 - T_1)}$$
$$\mathbf{\Delta_r U^\circ (T_2) - \Delta_r U^\circ (T_1) = \Delta C_v^\circ (T_2 - T_1)}$$
where $\Delta C_p^\circ = \sum \nu_p C_{p,m}^\circ (\text{products}) - \sum \nu_r C_{p,m}^\circ (\text{reactants})$.

quickRevision: Monatomic: C_v = 3/2 R, C_p = 5/2 R, γ = 1.67.
Diatomic: C_v = 5/2 R, C_p = 7/2 R, γ = 1.40.
Kirchhoff's law: Δ_r H°(T₂) - Δ_r H°(T₁) = ΔC_p° (T₂ - T₁).
keyFormulae: Δ_r H°(T₂) - Δ_r H°(T₁) = ΔC_p° (T₂ - T₁)
